pr_title: RenderManager: improve VideoPicture comparison for HDR
pr_body:
## Description
RenderManager: improve VideoPicture comparison for HDR videos

Fix https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/24166

## Motivation and context
While working on https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/26021 found that only are compared limited fields of VideoPicture and nothing related to HDR type or metadata.

With this PR also triggers render re-configure e.g. if switching to video with same dimensions and fps but different HDR type or even same HDR type but different display metadata or light metadata.

Also added color_primaries and color_transfer comparison.
 
## How has this been tested?
Runtime Windows playing different videos without stop previous video.

Specifically tested the case of 4K video with same HDR type (HDR10) but different metadata.

## What is the effect on users?
Fixes some issues like https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/24166 if different video is playback without stopping previous and videos has different HDR metadata or in case of SDR videos different color primaries, etc.

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
<!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->

1. Play sample video 1

3. Stop the playback of video 2

This is an automatically generated message. If you believe it was sent in error, please say so and a team member will remove the "Ignored rules" label.

I followed your instructions to reproduce the problem using your sample files and don't see any difference. Do you have alternate sample files that are more obvious to try? I don't know if Kodi's built-in screenshot feature supports HDR but if so, maybe it'd help if you took screenshots. The only thing I noticed was when I played the second file while the first one was playing, the HDR popup icon on my tv didn't popup. But, if the tv is already in HDR mode, I don't think it would.

I tested using Kodi 21.0b1-Omega-r64480-git+22a988aad3 running on Debian Linux, connected to an LG OLED tv.

> I don't know if Kodi's built-in screenshot feature supports HDR but if so, maybe it'd help if you took screenshots.

This how the video 2 looks when it was started "normally":

![IMG_20231209_172858](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/28512968/8abe7e50-efbf-446b-a13a-57d44ed3d542)

This is when that same video 2 is started during the playback of video 1:

![IMG_20231209_172822](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/28512968/b50fe6b1-9f2f-4942-954f-169a9e183078)

Notice almost no grey squares on second photo. That's not because of a bad photo - that's how it actually looks.

The issue is happening only if the HDR video we are switching to has the same resolution/fps as the previous HDR video.  
This is "fixed" If I force renderer reconfigure, like this for example:

```
diff --git a/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoRenderers/RenderManager.cpp b/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoRenderers/RenderManager.cpp
index 7bf7fcc..92f35fd 100644
--- a/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoRenderers/RenderManager.cpp
+++ b/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoRenderers/RenderManager.cpp
@@ -93,7 +93,7 @@ bool CRenderManager::Configure(const VideoPicture& picture, float fps, unsigned
         m_height == picture.iHeight &&
         m_dwidth == picture.iDisplayWidth &&
         m_dheight == picture.iDisplayHeight &&
-        m_fps == fps &&
+        m_fps != fps &&
         m_orientation == orientation &&
         m_stereomode == picture.stereoMode &&
         m_NumberBuffers == buffers &&
```

ping @fritsch @a1rwulf @lrusak

This is not the proper fix. Idea of this function is to avoid reconfiguring (loosing frames) as good as possible. What you are doing here basically drives this aspect nuts.

Original use-case: Inpustream, e.g. netflix or LiveTV, commercial switch.

The real solution would be to check if initial hdr mode matches next hdr mode and if those change -> switch.
Of course this is not a proper fix. That's why I pinged you guys so you would figure out a proper one :smiley:

Got it :-).  Yeah - if we continues this behaviour to compare picture (new video) and local properties, we need to store HDR information inside the object and in the picture and add those to the comparison. This way we can reconfigure the moment those attributes change.
